entry.title: Regularization in Machine Learning — How to Actually Prevent Overfitting (L1, L2, Dropout)
entry.summary:
What is regularization in machine learning, and how do you actually prevent overfitting in practice? This guide explains L1 vs L2, dropout, and early stopping with real-world intuition and code. Cross-posted from Zeromath. Original article: https://zeromathai.com/en/regularization-generalization-en/ You train a model: training loss → near zero
validation loss → terrible
This is not a bug. It’s overfitting. Powerful models memorize by default. E_aug(w) = E_train(w) + λΩ(w) Fit the data, but control complexity. smooth weights
stable training
works almost everywhere
L1 Regularization
sparse weights
feature selection
L1 vs L2 (Quick Decision)
L1 → sparse
L2 → stable Stop when validation loss increases. early → generalization
late → memorization
Dropout
disables neurons randomly
reduces co-adaptation
Practical Setup (PyTorch)
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW( best_val = float("inf") for epoch in range(epochs): if val < best_val: best_val = val else: patience_counter += 1 if patience_counter > patience: break
Start with L2 (weight decay) Add early stopping If still overfitting → add dropout If sparsity needed → use L1 stacking dropout + strong L2 + early stopping together
assuming more regularization is always better
tuning λ without validation
Too much regularization = underfitting. Regularization is not about reducing error. It is about controlling model behavior. Overfitting is not a bug. It’s what models do by default. Regularization is how you control it. What worked best for you — weight decay, dropout, or early stopping?

entry.title: Optimization vs Regularization — The Real Reason Your Model Overfits (and How to Fix It)
entry.summary: Most deep learning problems are not architecture problems. They are training problems. Specifically: Optimization issues Missing regularization Cross-posted from Zeromath. Original article: https://zeromathai.com/en/dl-optimization-regularization-integrated-lecture-en/ Training loop: Compute gradient Update weights Repeat Real issues: Noisy gradients (minibatch) Complex loss landscape Different parameter scales Fix: Momentum → smoother updates RMSProp → adaptive step size Adam → default optimizer Too large: Loss explodes Too small: Training stalls Start high → decay over time Pattern: Training loss ↓ Validation loss ↓ then ↑ Meaning: Model memorized Generalization failed Goal: Stabilizes weights Sparse models Prevents dependency Stops over-training If model overfits: Add L2 Add dropout Use early stopping If model doesn’t learn: Check learning rate Try Adam Normalize inputs Optimization = engine Regularization = brakes You need both. Training longer always helps → ❌ Bigger model always better → ❌ Adam solves everything → ❌ Good models are not just trained. They are controlled. What helped your model the most? Learning rate tuning? Regularization? Optimizer choice? Let’s discuss.
